title: How Feedback Stabilizes a System
production_path_basis: The flagship explanation must work without narration or music.
audience: General engineering learners and introductory controls students
assumed_knowledge: a target value may differ from output
central_message: Feedback repeatedly measures output, compares it with a target, and changes the input.
takeaway: Closed-loop correction can reject a disturbance, but tuning shapes drop, overshoot, oscillation, and settling.
platform: website showcase and bundled desktop example
scientific_depth: introductory closed-loop feedback, PI action, actuator lag, disturbance rejection, and tuning tradeoffs
visual_direction: dark systems dashboard with stable signal colors and aligned response plots
pacing: physical hook, one signal cycle, one numerical correction, response, tuning, synthesis
constraints: use identical axes and disturbance time across cases
do not present the controller as production automotive design
success_criteria: every signal has a clear direction and meaning
open loop cannot reject the hill load
